question.text: A uniform magnetic field <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.3</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> is along the positive <math> <mtext>Z</mtext> </math> -direction. A rectangular loop (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>d</mi></math>) of sides <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi>cm</mi><mo>×</mo><mn>5</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi>cm</mi></math> carries a current <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>I</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>. Out of the following different orientations which one corresponds to stable equilibrium?

solution.text:
U=-M→·B→=-MBcosθ

For stable equilibrium potential energy should be minimum and τ=0

Umin=-MB    when θ=0°

⇒cos⁡θ = 1

⇒M→ and B→  are on same direction.
